_comment: The trades' headers: each Def*.cs in ServUO is a recipe table plus a
short header of overrides, and this is the headers. The tables are the
other files in this directory, one per `trade` named below.
ORDER IS THE ID. The index into `systems` is a SystemId, and it rides in a
`Crafting` component and in a save record. Append, never reorder.
`delay_ms` is ServUO's `Delay` in milliseconds; build.rs turns it into a
tick count and refuses one that is not a whole number of ticks. Omitted
fields take the defaults build.rs documents: 1250ms, one beat, no

systems.note: The chance floor is zero, so a recipe you have only just qualified for always fails at first; the exceptional curve is the sliding one, which is what makes the last five points of the skill worth having.
Half of everything a tailor qualifies for works first time, which is ServUO's `GetChanceAtMin` of 0.5 and the difference between a trade that is pleasant to learn and one that is not.
A smith's floor with a carpenter's freedom to work anywhere.
The only shipped system that takes the default exceptional curve — it overrides no ECA at all — which is why a flat sixty points appears here and nowhere else.
Bowcraft uses ServUO's fifty-percent floor and exceptional curve; it needs no workshop, only a carried fletcher's tool.
Cooking uses ServUO's zero-percent floor and sliding exceptional curve. Individual recipes require a mill, heat, or an oven as their ingredients demand.
